items.passage: Our coach did not come. Hedwig and I were left in the courtyard of the inn, where a stone fountain stood dry and full of leaves, and for want of other talk we spoke of Mr. Hemi's brother, whose fame as a builder of bridges had reached even Hedwig's village across the sea. I had admired him for years; I had copied his sketches into this very book. Then Hedwig, quite without malice, mentioned that the bridges were drawn by a clerk in his office, a man who died poor and unnamed. I said nothing for a long while. I find tonight that I cannot tear the copied sketches out, for the lines are still handsome, yet neither can I look at them as I did this morning. Hedwig, I think, regretted telling me, and offered me an orange from her basket by way of apology. We ate it slowly while the innkeeper swept the fountain's basin, raising a small brown cloud.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the reputation of Mr. Hemi's brother after hearing Hedwig's account?
options: She remains confident that Hedwig's account is a rumor spread out of envy.
She is unsettled by it, still valuing the work while losing her old regard for him.
She is relieved to have a reason to stop studying the sketches she once copied.
She is angry with Hedwig for spoiling a reputation that had pleased her for years.
items.explanation: 화자는 이야기를 듣고 오랫동안 말을 잃었고, 베낀 스케치를 찢지는 못하지만 아침처럼 바라볼 수도 없다고 말한다. 이 두 단서를 이어 보면 작품의 가치는 인정하면서도 인물에 대한 존경은 흔들린 상태임을 알 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 화자가 소문을 의심하는 장면이 없어 틀리고, C는 스케치를 버리지 못한다는 진술과 어긋난다. D는 Hedwig가 악의 없이 말했고 화자가 분노를 드러내지 않으므로 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Who decides which child stays behind when the olives must be carried down? So the old tellers on the terraces above Naples begin this tale. A young teacher named Emilio came to the hill school and announced that the slowest reader would stay to tend the trees while the others went to market. Alessia, who read slowly but counted quickly, folded her arms and said nothing. On market day Emilio found the baskets tallied wrong and the prices muddled, for no one else could reckon so well, and he climbed back up the hill red-faced to fetch her. The tellers say he never again chose by a single measure, though they add, with a wink, that he took a long time to admit it aloud. Even now, grandmothers who repeat the story pause here to slice bread, and the children wait, chins on hands, for the ending they already know.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Emilio?
options: Openly scornful, presenting him as a fool who never learns from his error
Deeply admiring, presenting his choice as wise from the very beginning
Gently amused, treating his mistake as forgivable while noting his pride
Coolly detached, reporting his actions without any hint of judgment
items.explanation: 서술자는 Emilio가 얼굴이 붉어진 채 언덕을 다시 올라왔다고 묘사하고, 그가 이후 하나의 기준으로 고르지 않았다고 하면서도 윙크와 함께 그것을 말로 인정하는 데 오래 걸렸다고 덧붙인다. 두 단서는 실수를 너그럽게 보면서도 자존심을 살짝 놀리는 태도를 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. A는 그가 교훈을 얻었다는 서술과 어긋나고, B는 처음 선택이 틀렸던 점을 무시한다. D는 윙크 같은 평가적 표현이 있어 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: On the Thursday after the funeral, Josiah carried his late teacher's violin case into the laundromat because he had nowhere else to sit while his shirts dried. Harriet, who conducted the youth orchestra, happened to be folding towels two machines away. She recognized the case at once. Everyone had expected the instrument to go to her, the old man's oldest student, not to a boy of fourteen who still rushed his scales. Josiah set it on his knees and said he would give it to her if she asked. Harriet considered the dented corners, the tape on the handle, the boy's hands. Then she asked him to play something, there among the spinning drums, and listened without correcting a single note. Later she told him which shop restrings old instruments cheaply. Outside, a bus hissed at the curb, and the steam from the dryer vents curled into the cold air above the street.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?
options: A young violinist plays music in a laundromat while waiting for his laundry to dry.
A conductor tries to persuade a student to return an instrument that belongs to her.
People should always respect the wishes of those who have recently passed away.
A woman who expected an inheritance comes to accept the boy who received it instead.
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분은 모두가 바이올린이 Harriet에게 갈 것이라 기대했다는 사실을 밝히고, 뒷부분에서 그녀는 돌려받는 대신 소년의 연주를 교정 없이 듣고 수리점까지 알려 준다. 이 대비를 연결하면 그녀가 소년을 정당한 주인으로 받아들인다는 요지가 드러나므로 D가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 그녀가 오히려 돌려받기를 원하지 않으므로 목적이 다르다. C는 지문이 다루지 않는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Three clothespins per shirt, two per towel, one per sock: Ximena had hung her family's laundry by these rules on the Cairo rooftop since she was eight. Tariq, the landlord's son, liked to watch her count them out from the stairwell. One afternoon the wind came hard off the desert, and he ran up to help, pinning sheets any way he could, sometimes with four pins, sometimes with none. Ximena nearly scolded him. Instead she watched the sheets snap and hold, and she noticed that not one had fallen. The next week she left a few towels hanging by a single pin, just to see. They dried as quickly as the others. Below the roof, a vendor called out the price of guavas, and pigeons settled in a row along the water tank.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?
options: A girl begins to loosen a strict routine after seeing it was less necessary than she believed.
A girl and a boy work together to keep the family laundry from blowing off a windy roof.
A boy learns from a girl the correct way to hang laundry so that it dries more quickly.
Helping one's neighbors during difficult weather is the best way to build a friendship.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Ximena는 여덟 살 때부터 정해진 개수의 빨래집게 규칙을 지켜 왔고, 바람 부는 날 Tariq이 아무렇게나 꽂은 시트가 하나도 떨어지지 않는 것을 본다. 뒷부분에서 그녀는 일부러 집게 하나로 수건을 걸어 보는데, 이 두 곳을 이으면 습관을 내려놓기 시작한다는 요지가 드러나 A가 정답이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 배우는 사람을 뒤바꿔 목적이 다르다. D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage:
Paper envelopes rustle as NASRIN sorts seeds at the long table of the Samarkand cooperative. AYDIN, her teacher, pins a hem on a dress hanging nearby.
AYDIN: Tell the inspector these melon seeds came from our own gardens. He will grant the stall without questions.
NASRIN: They came from the bazaar.
AYDIN: A small thing. The stall feeds both of us.
NASRIN: (labeling an envelope slowly) Last spring you made me unpick a whole sleeve because one stitch was crooked. You said a garment that lies about its seams will lie about everything.
AYDIN: (pausing, needle raised) I said that?
NASRIN: Twice.
(AYDIN sets the needle down and takes the envelope from her. She crosses out the word "ours" and writes "bazaar" in its place.)
AYDIN: Then the inspector may ask his questions.
(Outside, a cart rattles past, loaded with sacks of onions, and dust drifts through the open door.)
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the passage?
options: To describe how seeds are sorted, labeled, and sold at a cooperative stall
To show a mentor being held to her own principle by the student she taught
To show an apprentice losing her place after refusing to obey her teacher
To suggest that honesty is always rewarded in matters of trade and business
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Aydin은 씨앗 출처를 속이자고 제안하지만, Nasrin은 예전에 Aydin이 바느질 한 땀까지 정직해야 한다고 가르친 말을 되새긴다. 뒤에서 Aydin이 직접 라벨을 고쳐 쓰는 장면과 이를 이어 보면, 제자가 스승의 원칙으로 스승을 돌려세우는 장면이라는 목적이 드러나므로 B가 정답이다. A는 소재만 쓰고 목적이 다르며, C는 Nasrin이 자리를 잃는 내용이 없다. D는 보상 여부가 나오지 않는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Four trays of dough, two ovens, one hour before the doors open: that was the rule of the bakery in Kerala where Camille and I worked the summer after the storm. We had not spoken properly in years, Camille and I, though we kneaded at the same table. Kenji, the owner, assumed we were simply quiet people. Then the flood washed out the garden behind the shop and uncovered a tin box our grandmother had buried there, full of letters she had written to each of us and never sent. Camille read hers standing in the mud. I read mine by the ovens. Neither of us said what was inside. But the next morning she slid the sugar jar toward me before I asked for it, and I held the oven door for her tray. Kenji, noticing nothing, complained about the price of cardamom.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the passage?
options: To describe the daily schedule that two sisters followed while working in a bakery
To explain how a storm destroyed the garden behind a small bakery in Kerala
To show two distant sisters taking a first, wordless step toward each other
To argue that family secrets should always be revealed before it is too late
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자와 Camille은 같은 탁자에서 일하면서도 몇 년간 제대로 말하지 않았다고 하고, 뒷부분에서는 편지를 읽은 다음 날 말없이 설탕 병을 건네고 오븐 문을 잡아 준다. 두 곳의 대비를 이으면 소원했던 자매가 말없이 가까워지기 시작한다는 목적이 드러나 C가 정답이다. A는 일정만 다룬 소재 요약이고, B는 폭풍이라는 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르다. D는 지문이 주장하지 않는 일반적 교훈이다.

items.passage: A brass token, worn smooth, still sits in my coat pocket from the years I rode Nikos's bus to the open-air market in Istanbul. Every Saturday I bought figs from Fatma's stall, and every Saturday Nikos waited an extra minute at her corner so I could run back with the bag. When a new line opened across the city, offering better hours, his friends urged him to transfer. He laughed and said the new route had no figs on it. Fatma, for her part, refused a larger stall near the ferry because, she told me, her old customers would not find her there. I was young and thought them both foolish. Only years later, when I moved away and no driver knew my stop, did I understand what they had been keeping. Last month the market added a glass roof, and the pigeons now perch along its steel beams.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?
options: The narrator remembers buying figs every Saturday and riding a bus to the market.
Two workers lose good opportunities because they are afraid of unfamiliar places.
Loyalty to one's friends is always more valuable than money or personal success.
The narrator comes to value the steady loyalty that once seemed foolish to her.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Nikos와 Fatma는 더 나은 기회를 거절하고 오래된 손님 곁에 남으며, 화자는 당시 그들을 어리석다고 여겼다. 뒷부분에서 화자는 이사를 간 뒤에야 그들이 지키던 것을 이해했다고 말하므로, 두 곳을 이으면 D가 요지다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 같은 소재를 쓰지만 두려움이라는 다른 동기를 내세운다. C는 '항상'이라는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Chalk dust and the smell of the harbor still drift through this classroom in Marseille, Remy, and I am writing to you from my desk during the break. You will laugh, but I am learning French verbs at seventy so that I can finally read the street signs I have walked past my whole life. When Theo first came to my fish stall, he was lost and could not read them either. I drew him a map on a scrap of wrapping paper, with a fish where my stall was and a star for his school. He still carries it, though he knows the way now. Last week he copied the street names for me into a notebook, slowly, letter by letter, and quizzed me as I sorted the mackerel. Tell your mother the boats came in late this morning, and the gulls were louder than the teacher.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the letter?
options: To show how an old man and a boy have each guided the other in finding their way
To explain why the writer decided to sell fish near a language school in Marseille
To describe the route that Theo once followed from the fish stall to his school
To suggest that it is never too late for anyone to learn a new language or skill
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 길을 잃은 Theo에게 포장지에 지도를 그려 주었고, 뒷부분에서는 Theo가 거리 이름을 공책에 베껴 주며 화자에게 퀴즈를 낸다. 두 일화를 이으면 노인과 소년이 서로에게 길잡이가 되어 준다는 목적이 드러나므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 없는 이유를 내세우고, C는 지도 일화만 요약한 것이다. D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Jeju Island, the tellers say, once had an orchard no one tended, and at its edge stood a shop that sold ribbons and candles. Each spring a man named Cormac came to the shopkeeper, Sunja, asking for the finest candle she had to mark the day he and his late wife had planted the first tangerine tree there. Each spring Sunja sold him one, and each spring he left it burning on a stump while the trees went wild around him. In the seventh year she refused. She handed him a pruning knife instead and walked with him into the tangled rows. Together they cut back one tree until light reached its lowest branches. The next spring Cormac bought no candle at all, and he arrived with his own knife and a basket. Sunja, the tellers add, raised her prices on ribbons that year, and no one could say why.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the passage?
options: A shopkeeper sells a grieving customer a candle every spring for many years.
A man learns to honor a memory by caring for what it left behind, not by ritual alone.
A shopkeeper refuses to sell candles because she wishes to protect the orchard.
Every loss should be remembered with patience, kindness, and steady hard work.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Cormac은 매년 초를 사서 그루터기에 켜 두지만 과수원은 방치된 채 거칠어진다. 뒷부분에서 Sunja가 초 대신 전지 칼을 건네고, 다음 해 Cormac이 초 없이 칼과 바구니를 들고 오므로, 두 곳을 이으면 의식보다 남겨진 것을 돌보는 방식으로 기억을 기린다는 요지가 드러나 B가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, C는 같은 소재로 거절의 목적을 잘못 짚었다. D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: "You going to finish that boat, or just sit with it?" Devon called from the end of the dock. Amelie did not answer. The half-built skiff had rested on two sawhorses beside the lake for nine summers, ever since she and Devon had begun it together and then quarreled over the shape of the bow. Neither had touched it since, though both still walked past it most evenings. This evening Amelie had brought a plane and a jar of nails. She ran her hand along the bow, the curve Devon had wanted, and did not reshape it. When he came closer, she held out a second hammer, handle first, and waited. Out on the water, a heron lifted from the reeds and flew low toward the cypress trees.
items.question: Based on the passage, why does Amelie most likely hold out a second hammer to Devon?
options: She hopes to resume the shared project and mend the old quarrel with him.
She wants to prove that the boat's bow was built correctly from the start.
She is irritated by his remark and wants him to do the hardest work himself.
She needs the boat finished quickly before the lake's summer season ends.
items.explanation: 지문은 두 사람이 뱃머리 모양으로 다툰 뒤 아홉 해 동안 배를 건드리지 않았다고 밝히고, Amelie가 Devon이 원했던 곡선을 고치지 않은 채 쓰다듬는 장면을 보여 준다. 이 두 단서를 이으면 그녀가 화해하고 함께 작업을 이어 가려 한다는 동기가 드러나므로 A가 정답이다. B는 결과처럼 보이는 정당성 입증을 동기로 착각했고, C는 짜증이라는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기다. D는 지문에 없는 외부 시간 압박을 끌어왔다.

items.passage: Two buses an hour climbed past the stop on the ridge road outside Lagos, and Sergio had already let three of them go. The letter in his pocket offered him a place on a club in another city, where he would start every match instead of watching from the bench. Nneka, his coach, sat beside him on the concrete bench, saying nothing about it. She had benched him all season for missing practices, and he had called her unfair in front of the team. Yet that morning she had written to the other club herself, praising his speed and his footwork. Sergio had seen the copy on her desk. When the fourth bus came, he stood, shook her hand for a long moment, and boarded. Nneka watched it disappear around the bend, then walked back down to sweep the training field.
items.question: Based on the passage, why does Sergio most likely shake Nneka's hand for a long moment before boarding?
options: He wants to show her that he has forgiven her for keeping him on the bench all season.
He has realized she helped him get the offer, and he wishes to thank her for it.
He hopes the gesture will persuade her to let him return to the team's first lineup.
He is nervous about the new club and wants to delay leaving the familiar bus stop.
items.explanation: 지문은 Sergio가 코치를 불공평하다고 비난했던 과거를 밝힌 뒤, 그녀가 직접 상대 클럽에 추천서를 썼고 Sergio가 그 사본을 보았다고 서술한다. 두 단서를 이으면 그가 코치의 도움을 깨닫고 고마움을 표한다는 동기가 드러나므로 B가 정답이다. A는 용서라는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기이고, C는 그가 떠나는 결과와 맞지 않는 선발 복귀를 끌어왔다. D는 지문에 근거가 없는 불안을 동기로 내세웠다.

items.passage:
JOON stands behind the counter of his clock shop in Busan, oiling a gear. GYEONGHO, his stepdaughter, enters with her school bag.
GYEONGHO: You fixed Mother's alarm clock. It rang this morning for the first time in a year.
JOON: It needed a new spring.
GYEONGHO: I broke it. The night I shouted that you would never be my father, I threw it at the wall.
JOON: (setting down the gear) I know. I found it under your bed when I was painting.
GYEONGHO: You never said anything.
JOON: (taking a folded letter from the drawer, never sealed) I tried. This was supposed to say I was sorry for the things I shouted back. I could not find the right words, so I fixed what I could fix.
(He hands her the letter. She does not open it but puts it in her bag.)
JOON: Now, help me hang this pendulum. The customer comes at four.
items.question: Based on the passage, why did Joon most likely repair the alarm clock?
options: He wanted to make Gyeongho confess that she was the one who broke it.
He hoped a working clock would help Gyeongho wake up on time for school.
He offered the repair as an apology he had been unable to put into words.
He was required by her mother to restore every object damaged in the house.
items.explanation: Joon은 사과 편지를 쓰려 했지만 끝내 봉하지 못했다고 밝히고, 적절한 말을 찾지 못해 고칠 수 있는 것을 고쳤다고 말한다. 이 두 대사를 이어 읽으면 시계 수리가 말로 하지 못한 사과였다는 동기가 드러나므로 C가 정답이다. A는 자백이라는 결과를 동기로 착각했고, B는 실용적 이유라는 다른 동기다. D는 지문에 없는 어머니의 요구라는 외부 원인을 끌어왔다.

items.passage: When I was twelve, I broke my father's bicycle chain on a Dhaka curb and carried the pieces to Hari's shoe repair stall, because Hari could mend anything with leather and wire. I had already rehearsed a story about a careless rickshaw driver. Hari listened, nodding, then asked me to hold the chain while he worked. As he threaded each link, he told me how, as a boy, he had blamed a stray dog for a torn sandal and how his own father had believed him for thirty years. "He still mentions that dog," Hari said. "I have never had the courage to correct him." That evening I told my father the chain broke because I had jumped the curb too fast. He sighed, and then he laughed. Outside our window the street vendors were packing up their carts of mangoes for the night.
items.question: Based on the passage, why does Putri most likely tell her father the truth about the chain?
options: She fears that Hari will report the accident to her father if she does not.
She wants her father to laugh with her about how foolishly she had ridden.
She is upset that the rickshaw driver would be blamed and punished unfairly.
Hari's story shows her the lasting weight of a lie that is never corrected.
items.explanation: 화자 Putri는 인력거꾼 탓을 하는 이야기를 미리 연습해 두었지만, Hari가 어린 시절 개를 탓한 거짓말을 삼십 년 동안 바로잡지 못했다고 고백하는 것을 듣는다. 두 단서를 이으면 바로잡지 않은 거짓말의 무게를 깨닫고 진실을 말했다는 동기가 드러나므로 D가 정답이다. A는 Hari가 고자질할 근거가 없는 외부 원인이고, B는 아버지가 웃은 결과를 동기로 착각했다. C는 꾸며 낸 인력거꾼에 대한 다른 감정을 동기로 내세웠다.

items.passage: Oaxaca was dry that March, and the river we crossed to reach my grandmother's village was only stones and cracked mud. Halfway across, Esperanza stopped and asked me to say my full name aloud. I said Eulalio, the name on my school papers, the name everyone used. She shook her head and told me the other one, the name of her own brother, which my parents had written second on my birth record and then forgotten. He had drowned in this same river, she said, in a year when it ran high. Then she made me repeat his name three times, standing on the stones where the water used to be, until she was satisfied that I would not lose it. I did not understand her then. At the far bank, a boy was selling cold tamarind drinks from a cooler, and we each bought one.
items.question: Based on the passage, why does Esperanza most likely make Eulalio repeat the second name?
options: She wants the memory of her drowned brother to be carried on by her grandson.
She is annoyed that Eulalio uses only the name written on his school papers.
She believes saying the name will protect the boy from the river's floodwaters.
She plans to have the boy's school records changed to show his second name.
items.explanation: Esperanza는 손자의 두 번째 이름이 자신의 오빠 이름이며 그가 바로 이 강에서 익사했다고 밝힌다. 이어서 그녀는 손자가 이름을 잃지 않으리라 확신할 때까지 세 번 반복하게 하므로, 두 단서를 이으면 오빠에 대한 기억을 손자가 이어 가길 바란다는 동기가 드러나 A가 정답이다. B는 짜증이라는 다른 감정을 끌어왔고, C는 지문에 없는 미신적 이유다. D는 학교 서류라는 단어를 쓰지만 지문에 없는 계획을 동기로 삼았다.

items.passage: "Translate only what I say, nothing more," Somchai told me the first day, and so I have, Mother, for six weeks in this printing room in Chiang Mai. Yesterday the investors asked him who had designed the new type press. Somchai looked at the young mechanic oiling the rollers, then said the design was his own. I knew otherwise; I had seen the mechanic's drawings pinned above his bench. Later Somchai explained, quietly, that the mechanic's family owes money to the very men who were asking, and that a name on a patent would bring them knocking. I translated his claim exactly as he spoke it. I said nothing about the drawings, though my face burned. This morning the presses are running early, and the whole room smells of ink and wet paper. Please send the recipe for the mango rice.
items.question: Based on the letter, why does the writer most likely keep silent about the mechanic's drawings?
options: She wants Somchai to receive full credit so that he will keep employing her.
She understands that revealing the truth could expose the mechanic to danger.
She is embarrassed that she had looked at drawings she was not meant to see.
She expects the investors will learn the truth from the printed patent anyway.
items.explanation: Somchai는 처음부터 말한 것만 통역하라고 했지만, 결정적 단서는 그가 나중에 정비공의 가족이 바로 그 투자자들에게 빚이 있어 특허에 이름이 오르면 위험해진다고 설명한 부분이다. 화자가 얼굴이 달아오르면서도 침묵했다는 서술과 이를 이으면 정비공을 보호하려는 동기가 드러나 B가 정답이다. A는 자기 이익이라는 지문에 없는 동기이고, C는 달아오른 얼굴을 다른 감정으로 잘못 해석했다. D는 특허라는 단어를 쓰지만 근거 없는 예측을 끌어왔다.

items.passage: I found the letters on the third day the snow kept us in the cabin above Beirut. They were tucked beneath the lining of my grandfather's desk drawer, all addressed to Noor, his oldest friend, who was staying with us until the roads cleared. In them my grandfather confessed that he had taken credit for a poem Noor wrote when they were students, a poem that won him his first post. Noor sat by the stove, knitting, while I read. I waited until evening, then placed the bundle on her lap without a word. She read the first page and smiled sadly, as if she already knew. I had watched her for two days refusing to speak ill of anyone, even the neighbor who had cheated her on firewood, and I could not bear for her to be kept from the apology meant for her. Later we melted snow for tea.
items.question: Based on the passage, why does Faris most likely give the letters to Noor?
options: He wants to expose his grandfather's dishonesty so that others will judge him.
He hopes Noor will finally confront the neighbor who cheated her on firewood.
He believes Noor deserves to receive the apology his grandfather wrote to her.
He wants to learn whether Noor had known the truth about the poem all along.
items.explanation: Faris는 할아버지가 Noor의 시를 도용한 일을 고백한 편지들이 모두 Noor 앞으로 쓰였다는 사실을 발견한다. 또 그는 남을 나쁘게 말하지 않는 Noor를 지켜보며 그녀에게 온 사과를 막고 싶지 않았다고 말하므로, 두 단서를 이으면 C가 정답이다. A는 폭로하려는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기이고, D는 Noor가 이미 알고 있었다는 결과를 동기로 착각했다. B는 장작 이웃이라는 단어를 쓰지만 지문에 없는 목적을 끌어왔다.

items.passage: Isadora had sold her pies at the roadside diner outside Porto Alegre for twenty years, and the spring her daughter Maya was to marry, a travel magazine named them the best on the southern highway. Customers lined up before dawn. Isadora baked through the nights and still could not keep up, and the wedding plans lay untouched beneath a sack of flour. One evening she hung a sign on the door: closed for ten days, family matters. Regulars grumbled; a reporter called twice. Maya found her mother at the kitchen table with the guest list, which she had not looked at in weeks. Isadora remembered aloud how her own mother had missed her wedding to cover a shift, and how the empty chair still seemed to stand in every photograph. The folktale tellers say the pies tasted better when the diner reopened, though the recipe never changed.
items.question: Based on the passage, why does Isadora most likely close the diner for ten days?
options: She is exhausted by the crowds and wants to rest before reopening the diner.
She hopes the closing will make her pies more famous with eager customers.
She resents the magazine for bringing reporters who keep calling the diner.
She refuses to let her success keep her from her daughter's wedding as well.
items.explanation: 지문은 갑작스러운 성공으로 Isadora가 밤새 굽느라 결혼 준비가 밀가루 자루 밑에 방치되었다고 서술한다. 이어서 그녀는 자기 어머니가 근무 때문에 결혼식에 오지 못해 사진마다 빈 의자가 남은 일을 떠올리므로, 두 단서를 이으면 같은 일을 반복하지 않으려는 동기가 드러나 D가 정답이다. A는 피로라는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기이고, B는 재개장 후 파이가 더 맛있었다는 결과를 동기로 착각했다. C는 기자라는 단어를 쓰지만 지문에 없는 원망을 끌어왔다.

items.passage: Ayesha did not trust her new hire. Lanying had joined the galley crew at the Karachi docks only a week earlier, and already she had reorganized the spice shelves and asked why the cooks worked double shifts while the officers' steward worked none. Ayesha had worked those double shifts for eleven years. She had missed her son's school prizes and her mother's last birthday for them. Now, chopping onions beside the girl, she felt the old resentment stir, and beneath it something less familiar, a small flicker of hope that someone might finally say aloud what she had swallowed. She caught herself watching Lanying's quick hands with something close to pride. Still she said only, "Mind the knife," and pushed the cutting board an inch farther away. The ship's engine shuddered beneath them, and the pots swung on their hooks.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the passage?
options: Wary resentment tinged with a reluctant, growing hope
Quiet hope that is only slightly shadowed by suspicion
Reluctant hope expressed through a gentle, open warmth
Weary exhaustion caused by long years of shipboard work
items.explanation: 지문은 Ayesha가 새 직원을 믿지 않고 오랜 희생에 대한 원망이 되살아난다고 서술하면서, 그 아래 누군가 자신이 삼켜 온 말을 해 줄지 모른다는 작은 희망을 함께 보여 준다. 마지막까지 짧은 경고만 하고 도마를 밀어내는 태도를 보면 경계와 원망이 더 두드러지므로 A가 정답이다. B는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었고, C는 덜 두드러진 희망만 강조하며 드러난 따뜻함을 과장했다. D는 소재와 어울리지만 지문의 단서가 약한 어조다.

items.passage: Bamboo ribs lay drying in rows across the kite-maker's yard in Hanoi when Chinedu, the mayor, came to say the clinic would close. The town could not pay for it, he told Budi, its only doctor, and he had signed the order that morning. Budi said nothing at first. He picked up a half-finished kite and tested its frame, as he did when patients told him bad news. Chinedu went on listing reasons, more of them than were needed, and his voice grew softer with each one. Twice he glanced at the children chasing a red kite above the wall, the same children Budi had treated for fever in the rainy season. At last he folded the order into his pocket rather than handing it over, and asked how much paper a kite like that would need. Overhead, the red kite dipped, caught a gust, and climbed.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall mood of the passage?
options: Lighthearted and playful, with only a brief moment of seriousness
Tense and somber, gradually giving way to a quiet, uncertain hope
Hopeful and confident, with a slight undercurrent of tension
Bitter and accusatory, reflecting the doctor's anger at the mayor
items.explanation: 지문은 병원 폐쇄 소식, Budi의 침묵, 필요 이상으로 이유를 늘어놓는 시장의 모습으로 긴장되고 무거운 분위기를 이어 간다. 그러다 시장이 아이들을 바라보고 명령서를 건네지 않은 채 주머니에 넣는 장면에서 조용하고 불확실한 희망이 나타나므로 B가 정답이다. C는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었고, A는 연 날리는 아이들이라는 덜 두드러진 요소만 본 것이다. D는 소재와 어울리지만 Budi가 분노를 드러내는 단서가 약하다.

items.passage:
By four o'clock the kiln had cooled enough to open,
and Hollis stood with her hand on its iron door
while Grant, the delivery boy, argued about the boxes:
ten, he said, not twelve; the invoice was wrong.
She argued back as if the count could matter,
as if the clay her husband wedged each spring
were not still drying, unfinished, on his shelf.
Grant raised his voice; she raised hers higher.
Between them, frost was gathering on the window,
and the bowls inside the kiln, still warm,
held the last glaze he had mixed, a blue
she had not dared to open all winter.
When Grant fell silent, she pulled the door.
Steam rose. One bowl had cracked along the rim.
The others shone. She counted them aloud,
softly, twice, and signed for ten.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the poem?
options: Irritable and combative, with grief appearing only in a single brief image
Calm and accepting, as the speaker finally makes peace with a quiet loss
Grief-laden beneath a surface of petty irritation that slowly gives way
Nostalgic and fond, focused on happy memories of a shared craft
items.explanation: 시는 상자 개수를 두고 다투는 짜증 섞인 표면 아래에, 선반 위에서 마르고 있는 남편의 미완성 점토와 겨우내 열지 못한 그의 마지막 유약이라는 슬픔의 단서를 여러 곳에 둔다. 다툼이 잦아들고 그녀가 부드럽게 그릇을 세며 열 개에 서명하는 장면까지 이으면 슬픔이 더 두드러진 어조이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었고, B는 끝부분의 차분함만 본 덜 두드러진 정서다. D는 도예라는 소재와 어울리지만 행복한 추억의 단서가 약하다.
